screenplay.text:
THE LIGHTHOUSE INSPECTOR

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

         1     EXT. COASTAL ROAD - DAY                                 1

               A white bakkie bounces along a dirt road between fynbos and
               sand dunes. Ahead, on a headland of black rock, stands a red
               and white LIGHTHOUSE.

         2     INT./EXT. WHITE BAKKIE - MOVING - DAY                   2

               MS. NAIDOO (40s), neat grey suit, clipboard on the passenger
               seat, drives with both hands on the wheel. A lanyard reads
               MARITIME SAFETY.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                               (into her phone, on
                               speaker)
                         One last inspection, then I
                         recommend it for automation. It's a
                         formality.

                                     SUPERVISOR (V.O.)
                         Be kind to the old man. He's been
                         there thirty-two years.

         3     EXT. LIGHTHOUSE - DOOR - DAY                            3

               A heavy green door. Ms. Naidoo knocks. Wind tugs at her
               jacket.

               The door opens. MR. FORTUIN (70s), wool jersey with holes at
               the elbows, white whiskers, holds a mug of tea.

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                         You're early. The kettle has only
                         just boiled.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                         I'm here to inspect the light, Mr.
                         Fortuin. Not to drink tea.

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                         Nobody inspects anything properly
                         without tea.

         4     INT. LIGHTHOUSE - STAIRWELL - CONTINUOUS                4

               An iron spiral staircase winds up and up. Ms. Naidoo climbs,
               counting under her breath. Mr. Fortuin climbs behind her,
               slowly, one hand on the rail.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                         One hundred and twelve steps. Every
                         night?

                                                            (CONTINUED)






                                                                       2.


               CONTINUED:

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                         Twice. Up to light it, up again at
                         midnight to check it. My knees have
                         opinions about it.

         5     INT. LIGHTHOUSE - LAMP ROOM - DAY                       5

               A round glass room full of sky. In the centre sits the great
               LENS, rings of cut glass taller than a man, catching the
               daylight in rainbows.

               Ms. Naidoo opens her clipboard. Mr. Fortuin polishes the
               lens with a soft yellow cloth.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                         A motor and a sensor could do all
                         of this. No stairs. No knees.

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                         A sensor can't see a boat in
                         trouble.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                         There is a radio for that now.

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                               (still polishing)
                         The radio only hears the boats that
                         call.

               She writes something down. He doesn't ask what.

         6     EXT. LIGHTHOUSE - GALLERY - DUSK                        6

               A narrow iron balcony circles the lamp room. The sea has
               turned dark and rough. Clouds pile up on the horizon.

               Ms. Naidoo looks out through a pair of binoculars. She
               stops. She looks again.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                         There. Something's out there. Past
                         the rocks.

               Mr. Fortuin takes the binoculars. Far out, a small fishing
               boat rolls in the swell. No lights on it.

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                         Their engine's gone. They'll drift
                         onto the reef.










                                                                       3.


         7     INT. LIGHTHOUSE - LAMP ROOM - CONTINUOUS                7

               Mr. Fortuin pulls a lever. Gears clank. The great lens
               begins to turn and the light blooms on, sweeping out across
               the water.

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                         Get the radio. Channel sixteen.
                         Tell the rescue station: two miles
                         south of the light, drifting west.

               Ms. Naidoo grabs the handset from the wall.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                               (into the radio)
                         Rescue station, rescue station,
                         this is the lighthouse. Fishing
                         boat adrift, two miles south,
                         drifting west, no lights!

                                     RESCUE OFFICER (V.O.)
                         Received, lighthouse. Launching
                         now. Keep your light on them.

               Mr. Fortuin cranks a small handle on the side of the lamp.
               The beam slows and holds on the boat.

         8     EXT. SEA - NIGHT                                        8

               The lighthouse beam pins the little fishing boat in white
               light. An orange RESCUE BOAT bounces over the waves toward
               it.

         9     INT. LIGHTHOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT                       9

               A tiny kitchen at the foot of the tower. Two mugs of tea on
               an oilcloth table. Ms. Naidoo's clipboard lies beside them.

               She tears the top page off, folds it, and drops it in the
               stove. It catches and curls.

                                     MS. NAIDOO
                         I'll need to come back next year.
                         For a second inspection.

                                     MR. FORTUIN
                               (pouring)
                         Come in the evening. The tea is
                         better.

                                                            FADE TO BLACK.

shots.source: A white bakkie bounces along a dirt road between fynbos and sand dunes. Ahead, on a headland of black rock, stands a red and white LIGHTHOUSE.
shots.rationale: Establishes the setting and the vehicle's position relative to the lighthouse at the start of the scene.

shots.source: MS. NAIDOO (40s), neat grey suit, clipboard on the passenger seat, drives with both hands on the wheel. A lanyard reads MARITIME SAFETY.
shots.rationale: Establishes the driver's focused presence before the conversation begins.

shots.source: One last inspection, then I recommend it for automation. It's a formality.
shots.rationale: Captures the intensity of her spoken recommendation to the unseen supervisor.

shots.source: Be kind to the old man. He's been there thirty-two years.
shots.rationale: Presents the voice of authority as a disembodied presence guiding the inspection.

shots.source: A heavy green door. Ms. Naidoo knocks. Wind tugs at her jacket.
shots.rationale: Establishes the lighthouse exterior and Ms. Naidoo's entrance before the door opens.

shots.source:
The door opens. MR. FORTUIN (70s), wool jersey with holes at the elbows, white whiskers, holds a mug of tea.
You're early. The kettle has only just boiled.
shots.rationale: Captures the dialogue exchange as Mr. Fortuin opens the door and offers tea.

shots.source: I'm here to inspect the light, Mr. Fortuin. Not to drink tea.
shots.rationale: Focuses on Ms. Naidoo's resolute response, emphasizing her purpose over the offered tea.

shots.source: Nobody inspects anything properly without tea.
shots.rationale: Frames the final line reinforcing the ritual of tea before any inspection begins.

shots.source: An iron spiral staircase winds up and up. Ms. Naidoo climbs, counting under her breath. Mr. Fortuin climbs behind her, slowly, one hand on the rail.
shots.rationale: Establishes the daunting vertical space and both characters at the start of their climb.

shots.source: One hundred and twelve steps. Every night?
shots.rationale: Allows close attention to Ms. Naidoo's counting line without distraction.

shots.source: Twice. Up to light it, up again at midnight to check it. My knees have opinions about it.
shots.rationale: Isolates Mr. Fortuin's weary response to highlight his physical perspective.

shots.source:
A round glass room full of sky. In the centre sits the great LENS, rings of cut glass taller than a man, catching the daylight in rainbows.
Ms. Naidoo opens her clipboard. Mr. Fortuin polishes the lens with a soft yellow cloth.
shots.rationale: Establishes the lighthouse lamp room and introduces both characters as they begin their task.

shots.source:
A motor and a sensor could do all of this. No stairs. No knees.
A sensor can't see a boat in trouble.
There is a radio for that now.
shots.rationale: Captures the dialogue exchange about automation versus human observation.

shots.source:
The radio only hears the boats that call.
She writes something down. He doesn't ask what.
shots.rationale: Focuses on Mr. Fortuin's hands and expression as he delivers the final line about the radio's limits.

shots.source:
A narrow iron balcony circles the lamp room. The sea has turned dark and rough. Clouds pile up on the horizon.
Ms. Naidoo looks out through a pair of binoculars. She stops. She looks again.
shots.rationale: Establishes the isolated lighthouse gallery at dusk as the characters begin their vigil.

shots.source:
There. Something's out there. Past the rocks.
Mr. Fortuin takes the binoculars. Far out, a small fishing boat rolls in the swell. No lights on it.
shots.rationale: Captures the moment of discovery as Ms. Naidoo points out the distant vessel.

shots.source: Their engine's gone. They'll drift onto the reef.
shots.rationale: Tightens on Mr. Fortuin's concern for the drifting boat's fate.

shots.source: Mr. Fortuin pulls a lever. Gears clank. The great lens begins to turn and the light blooms on, sweeping out across the water.
shots.rationale: Establishes the lighthouse interior and Mr. Fortuin's action of activating the light as the scene's inciting moment.

shots.source:
Get the radio. Channel sixteen. Tell the rescue station: two miles south of the light, drifting west.
Ms. Naidoo grabs the handset from the wall.
shots.rationale: Captures the dialogue exchange where the radio instructions are given and the handset is passed.

shots.source: Rescue station, rescue station, this is the lighthouse. Fishing boat adrift, two miles south, drifting west, no lights!
shots.rationale: Focuses on Ms. Naidoo's urgent radio transmission, emphasizing the critical distress call.

shots.source: Received, lighthouse. Launching now. Keep your light on them.
shots.rationale: Presents the rescue officer's voice as an off-screen authority confirming the plan.

shots.source: Mr. Fortuin cranks a small handle on the side of the lamp. The beam slows and holds on the boat.
shots.rationale: Tracks Mr. Fortuin fine-tuning the lamp beam to keep it fixed on the drifting boat.

shots.source: The lighthouse beam pins the little fishing boat in white light. An orange RESCUE BOAT bounces over the waves toward it.
shots.rationale: A wide static shot establishes the lighthouse beam's isolation and the boat's vulnerability against the night sea.

shots.source:
A tiny kitchen at the foot of the tower. Two mugs of tea on an oilcloth table. Ms. Naidoo's clipboard lies beside them.
She tears the top page off, folds it, and drops it in the stove. It catches and curls.
shots.rationale: Establishes the cramped kitchen space and the shared ritual of tea before the conversation turns to departure.

shots.source: I'll need to come back next year. For a second inspection.
shots.rationale: Focuses on Ms. Naidoo's resolute expression as she commits the inspection to a future date.

shots.source: Come in the evening. The tea is better.
shots.rationale: Captures Mr. Fortuin's pouring gesture and the implied warmth of the tea he offers.
